\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S2-Q02, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Bohr model}, answer={5.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: Bohr model energy levels | steps: E = 13.6 Z\^{}2 (1/4 - 1/9) = 47.2 gives Z}]

\section*{TOAS papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S1-Q01, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=multi, subtopic={Photoelectric effect}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=solved, working={Stopping potential 2 V and $\hbar\omega=6.26$ eV give $\phi=4.26$ eV; $I=\tfrac12\epsilon_0cE_0^2$ times $A\sin30^\circ$ gives $9.9\times10^{-4}$ W; yield $=(6\,\mu\mathrm A/e)/(P/\hbar\omega)=0.038$; saturation current $\propto E_0^2$ gives $6\times(25/15)^2=16.67\,\mu$A}, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S3 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: photoelectric effect, intensity of an electromagnetic wave, quantum yield | steps: read the stopping potential and saturation current from the graph; work function from the photon energy; intensity from E0 and power on the tilted plate; yield from photon rate; scaling of saturation current}]
In given experiment on the photoelectric effect monochromatic plane wave of light falls on a metal plate of area 66.3 cm$^2$ at angle $30^\circ$ as shown. Electric field in light wave varies according to $E=E_0\cos(\omega t+\phi_0)$ where amplitude $E_0=15$ V/m, angular frequency is $\omega=9.5\times10^{15}$ rad/s. Dependence of photoelectric current $I$ on voltage applied $V$ between the electrodes is shown by graph. Select the correct statement (s).
\bfig{119.0}{TOAS18_p1_phy_s1_q01_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Work function of metal plate is 4.26 eV.}
\opt{B}{Power received be metal plate by radiation is $9.9\times10^{-4}$ W.}
\opt{C}{Quantum yield (photoelectric efficiency) in the experiment is 0.038.}
\opt{D}{If amplitude of electric field in incident light is made 25 V/m then saturation current will become 16.67 $\mu$A.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=multi, subtopic={de Broglie waves}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=solved, working={(A) same $m$ and $\lambda$ give same $p$ and KE; (B) equal and opposite momenta; (C) $p^2/2m=hc/\lambda$ gives $\lambda_{dB}=\sqrt{h\lambda/2mc}$; (D) $r=p/qB$ gives $r_p:r_\alpha=2:1$}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: de Broglie wavelength, momentum and energy relations | steps: equal mass and wavelength; equal and opposite momenta in an explosion; energy absorbed by a free electron; radius ratio in a magnetic field}]

\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If two particle having same mass have same De-Broglie wavelength then they have same kinetic energy and same momentum.}
\opt{B}{When a bomb at rest explodes into two unequal pieces then both pieces have same De-Brogli wavelength.}
\opt{C}{When a photon of wavelength $\lambda$ incident on a free electron at rest then it's De-Broglie wavelength becomes $\sqrt{\dfrac{h\lambda}{2mC}}$, where $m$ is mass of electron.}
\opt{D}{A proton and an alpha particle are moving along circular path under same uniform magnetic field, then ratio of radius will be 2 : 1 if they have same De-Broglie wavelength}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\opt{C}{the cut-off wavelength will reduce to half and the intensities of all the X-rays will decrease.}

\end{qoptions}

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S1-Q01, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=single, subtopic={Bohr model}, answer={D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: Bohr quantisation with a modified potential | steps: force from the potential; quantisation of angular momentum; kinetic energy versus n}]
A hypothetical e-nucleus system obeys bohr's postulates and it's potential energy is expressed as $U=-\dfrac{K}{4r^4}$, where $K$ is positive constant then dependency of kinetic energy on principal quantum number $n$ is:

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S1-Q16, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=16, type=single, subtopic={de Broglie waves}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: de Broglie wavelength and energy loss | steps: momentum from the wavelength; kinetic energy at each point; energy lost; work of the resistance}]
In a cricket match, batsman hit the ball (mass $=m$) high in the air and fielding side player catch the ball near boundary. De broglie wavelength of ball just after hit from bat is $\lambda_1$ and just before the catch is $\lambda_2$. Assume height at which ball is hit by bat and height at which ball is catch are same. Find total work done by air-resistance (Mechanical energy is loss only due to air-resistance)
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{h^2}m\left(\dfrac1{\lambda_1}-\dfrac1{\lambda_2}\right)$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{h^2}{2m}\left(\dfrac1{\lambda_1^2}-\dfrac1{\lambda_2^2}\right)$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{h^2}{2m}\left(\dfrac{\lambda_1\lambda_2}{\lambda_1-\lambda_2}\right)$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{h^2}{2m}\left(\dfrac1{\lambda_1}-\dfrac1{-\lambda_2}\right)$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\opt{C}{increase the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons by a factor greater than two but and will have no effect on the magnitude of the photoelectric saturation current produced.}

\end{qoptions}

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S1-Q19, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=19, type=single, subtopic={X-rays}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I1 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: internal conversion in heavy atoms | steps: vacancy in an inner shell; subsequent emission}]
Internal conversion is the process whereby an excited nucleus transfers its energy directly to one of the most tightly bound atomic electrons, causing the electron to be ejected from the atom and leaving the atom in an excited state. The most probable process after an internal conversion from an atom with a high atomic number is that the
\begin{qoptions}

\opt{B}{atom emits one or several X-rays}
\opt{C}{nucleus emits a $\gamma$-ray}
\opt{D}{nucleus emits an electron}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS07-P1-PHY-S1-Q20, source={TNAS - Test 07 (20 Aug 2023)}, paper=1, qno=20, type=single, subtopic={Bohr model}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C2 F0}, diff_note={concepts: Bohr model of a hypothetical atom | steps: scaling of radius energy with charge and mass; energy of the levels; transition energy; photon momentum}]
In a hypothetical atom, a negatively charged particle having a charge of magnitude $3e$ and mass $3m$ revolves around a proton. Here, $e$ is the electronic charge and $m$ is the electronic mass. Mass of proton may be assumed to be much larger than that of the negatively charged particle, thus the proton is at rest. This ``atom'' obeys Bohr's postulate of quantization of angular momentum, that is $mvr=n\left(\dfrac h{2\pi}\right)$. It is given that for the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom: radius of orbit is $r_0$, speed of electron is $V_0$, and total energy is $-E_0$. The momentum of an emitted photon when it makes a transition from the second excited state to ground state, is
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{8E_0}c$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{E_0}c$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{24E_0}c$}
\opt{D}{None of these}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\opt{D}{Value of $q$ is $=6$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
